long_biography.plain_text:
Mark Getty began his career at Kidder Peabody in New York and Hambros Bank in London before co-founding Getty Images with Jonathan Klein in 1995. The venture consolidated fragmented stock-photography libraries and digitised their licensing, turning pooled Getty family capital into a major visual-content business. He served as executive chair for a decade and returned as board chair when Getty family shareholders resumed control in 2018.

Getty's economic story therefore has two distinct strands. His inherited wealth traces back to J. Paul Getty's oil fortune and the family trust, while Getty Images represents his own founder-led expansion into media. Alongside chairing the company, he oversees investments through Getty family entities. His public-service roles have included chairing the National Gallery in London and the British School at Rome, and he was appointed KBE for services to the arts.
